notes: §1985:VII.2.3.4 GR1: "all file control entries in the run unit which reference this file connector must have" the same OPTIONAL phrase, a consistent ASSIGN, a consistent RECORD DELIMITER implementor-name, the same RESERVE integer, the same organization, the same access mode and the same PADDING CHARACTER specification (items a to g). Implemented at 85: BinderDriver.Bind keys every EXTERNAL file by its external name and FileRegistry.Register keeps the first describer's connector, so the entries of a run unit share one file connector; Bind calls CheckExternalFileConsistency only under edition.DialectLevel >= 2023, so the 2023 additions (the same external FILE STATUS item) are not imposed at 85. Not implemented at 85: the agreement itself. FileEntryIdentity.Of builds an identity that holds items a to f, EmitExternalDescribes emits it, and ExternalTable.Describe compares it only under the EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH gate that CheckingFold.ExternalMaskAt folds from >>TURN, a directive --std 85 refuses (COBOL0900); no compile-time pass compares the entries of one compilation group. Item g cannot be compared at any edition: paddingCharacterClause is parsed and nothing is kept. Probed at 85: entries that differ in OPTIONAL and RESERVE, or in organization alone, compile and run in silence, the activated program served by the first describer's connector; entries that differ in organization and access mode end the run with an unhandled .NET exception (the repro). kb/Work PB5069 holds the mechanism, filed against §1985:VII.2.7.4 GR6 and §1985:VIII.2.4.4 GR8; it does not list this rule id and does not record the abnormal end. The witness runs two agreeing entries and writes in the called program a record the caller reads back.

next.reason: 1985 lists a-g for every file control entry of an external file connector: OPTIONAL, consistent ASSIGN, consistent RECORD DELIMITER, RESERVE, organization, access mode, and 'g. The same specification for the PADDING CHARACTER clause.' §2023:12.4.5.3 GR1 keeps a)-f) (c) now 'Either the STANDARD-1 phrase or a consistent value of feature-name-1') with the implementor's consistency rules documented (§2023:A.1 'FILE-CONTROL entry, ASSIGN clause (consistency rules for external file connectors)' and the RECORD DELIMITER item), drops the PADDING CHARACTER item (the clause is gone from 2023), and adds items no 1985 rule required, among them i) 'The same specification of the FILE STATUS clause, where data-name-4 shall reference the same corresponding external data item'. A 1985 run unit whose sequential entries for one external file name different FILE STATUS items no longer conforms: stricter.
